summary: Attorney-at-law Dexter Todd, acting for the three charged Transport and Harbours Department employees, is preparing a court challenge to the Director of Public Prosecutions' position that the criminal prosecution and the Commission of Inquiry may run concurrently. Todd argues a maritime casualty of this kind should be governed by the Guyana Shipping Act rather than common-law murder charges. Todd, who is also an APNU Member of Parliament, told a Thursday press conference: "None of the parties charged are to determine seaworthiness of that vessel. Seaworthiness of the vessel carries a particular procedure, and that has to be determined by, of course, MARAD." Captain Kevin Price is reported as having publicly stated the 87-year-old vessel lacked radar, an Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon, a functioning anchor and a search-and-rescue transponder. No other 31 July item makes this cumulative point. "It should be noted that no invitation was extended to the local media to cover the ceremony" — the 30 July swearing-in at State House was closed to the press; proceedings were streamed on President Ali's Facebook page and the link later shared with media by Director of Publ

The Guyana Congregational Union, in a statement issued Wednesday, extends condolences and says it hopes the newly appointed Commission will begin its work "very soon". The Union says it "trusts the panel's eventual findings and recommendations will bring some degree of comfort and satisfaction" to families and the wider public. The Union characterises the loss as unprecedented — Guyana has never suffered such a catastrophic loss of life in a single incident — and dwells on the deaths of young people and children.

The letter cites a Gazette Order dated 21 October 2025 assigning Minister of Public Works Juan Anthony Edghill responsibility for "Shipping and Harbour Services", and Cabinet Memorandum CP (2026) MOPW08/02 as the instrument under which he appointed the T&HD board. No other 31 July item cites these documents. The letter names the T&HD board as: Rosalinda Rasul (Chairperson, Head of Diaspora Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs); Yurlander Hughes (former Personnel Manager, now Acting General Manager); Annaser Hamilto

The letter argues by analogy from the Prairie Green Landfill search in Manitoba, Canada, for the remains of murdered Indigenous women Morgan Harris and Marcedes Myran — a search initially refused, then funded at CAD 20 million by Premier Wab Kinew, which recovered remains in late February 2025. It cites the earlier federal study concluding a search "could take three years and cost up to CAD 184 million (USD 128 million)" — the cost argument that was ultimately overridden.

The letter's central distinction: "It is not a question of criminal guilt but political accountability and moral responsibility." It calls for the resignation or dismissal of Ministers Deodat Indar and Juan Edghill, and holds President Ali responsible for not acting: "The President is not acting politically responsible by not firing the two Ministers. This is the first affected-community institutional position of its kind reported on 31 July. The resolutions followed a public meeting convened Wednesday by Toshao Terrence Domingo and councillors after their return from the 2026 National Toshaos Council Conference.

CMC-credited copy datelined Georgetown, Guyana, published 31 July. Mohamed is quoted: "The families want the vessel to float, and the families told me even if it is the bones themselves, they want the bones because it will bring some closure to them." Mohamed alleges the government resists salvage because of what would be found: "the anchor is not working, the electronic systems and only one engine was working. So that is their concern, how they will look." The piece flags this with "he alleged".

A one-hour OGGN Oil Talk podcast streamed live on 30 July on the Kaieteur Radio Guyana channel, hosted by Janette Bulkan with David Patterson, AFC shadow minister for public works and a former Minister of Public Works. Patterson, having held the ministry, treats annual certification of these vessels as routine — "how can you say you don't have the registration certificate... but you are certifying it every year" — which bears directly on the certificate no one has produced. He states the Transport and Harbours Department has not turned a profit since 2007 or 2009 and has not been officially audited since about 2005-2006. He cites Cap. 49:07 s. 18, under which inspectors of shipping may prevent overloaded vessels sailing and detain unfit ones. He argues the murder charges hollow out the inquiry because the operator's own management will also decline to self-incriminate, and predicts masters may refuse to sail. Bulkan puts the rescue timeline directly: first rescue at 2:27 a.m., more than three hours on. Auto-caption source; 92 per cent of the programme captured.
